description: P5.6 Conversation history / session management (Section 8.5) AND P5.7 App shell + navigation + least-privilege capabilities + README status flip. The history surface is the natural entry point that resumes a session (restoring persona, route pin, tags, enabled tools), and the app shell assembles all five surfaces and wires the single top-level CoreEvent subscription that fans events into the stores. Lands last because it depends on all prior surfaces being present. Depends on FEAT-001/002/003.
steps: HISTORY (src/features/history/): ConversationList (sorted/filtered index from state/conversations.ts: id, title, timestamps, tags, last route), SearchBar (client-side filter over title/tags), ConversationContextMenu (rename -> renameConversation; tag -> setConversationTags; duplicate -> createConversation seeded from the source's persona/pref/tags, or a dedicated command if FEAT-001 added one, else client-side re-create; export -> exportConversation(id, format) then trigger a download/save of the returned string; delete -> deleteConversation), SessionSummary (model usage/cost/tags derived from message usage + route metadata), NewConversationButton (createConversation).

HISTORY wiring: consume conversation_created / conversation_updated / conversation_deleted via the conversations store (invalidate + refresh the index). Resuming a session: openConversation(id) loads the full conversation; set it active and restore persona (assign already persisted), route pin (conversationPref), privacy tags, and enabledToolServers into the active-conversation state so the chat + model-selector + tool surfaces reflect the resumed session (Section 8.5).

APP SHELL (src/app.tsx + any layout components in src/components/): assemble the five surfaces into a navigable layout (e.g. a sidebar with History + a main pane hosting Chat with the Model selector in/near the Composer, and routes/tabs or panels for Tool manager and Agent editor). Establish ONE top-level onCoreEvent subscription (in a useEffect with a stable cleanup returning the UnlistenFn) that dispatches each CoreEvent to the relevant store's event-application function (fan-out), so surfaces stay in sync without each subscribing independently. Keep the existing app_version display or fold it into an about/status area if desired (do not break app.test.tsx, or update it to match).

CAPABILITIES (P5.7, crates/tauri-app/capabilities/default.json): update the description/comment to enumerate the full Phase 5 command set now exposed and reaffirm least privilege (Section 9.2). In Tauri v2, user #[tauri::command] handlers are authorized by generate_handler! registration, not by capability permission tokens, so keep permissions to `core:default` (no fs/shell/network granted to the webview) unless a specific built-in plugin is genuinely needed — if none is, do NOT add plugin permissions. Ensure the file stays valid JSON and consistent with the registered commands.

README: flip the Phase 5 line in the 'Implementation status' section (README.md line ~35) from 'PENDING' to 'DONE' following the existing PR #6 convention/wording used for Phases 0-4 (a 'DONE.' prefix + a short summary of what shipped: the five wired UI surfaces + any new commands/events).

TESTS (vitest + RTL): history — ConversationList renders and filters via SearchBar; context-menu actions call renameConversation/setConversationTags/exportConversation/deleteConversation; NewConversationButton calls createConversation; feed synthetic conversation_created/updated/deleted and assert the index refreshes; resume via openConversation restores persona/pin/tags/tools into active state. app shell — renders the surfaces; the single onCoreEvent subscription dispatches a synthetic event to the right store (assert a store transition); unlisten is called on unmount. Update app.test.tsx if the shell changed the app_version rendering. Mock invoke + listen.

FINAL LOCAL VERIFY: from hybrid-orchestrator/frontend run `NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check .` across the WHOLE frontend and fix any remaining formatting. Self-audit eslint/tsc across all new/changed files. In findings, report EXACTLY which frontend checks ran locally (prettier) vs deferred to CI (eslint/tsc/vitest) and why (node_modules uninstallable offline, npm 403).
acceptance_criteria: History surface lists/searches conversations, offers rename/tag/duplicate/export/delete via a context menu, shows a session summary and a new-conversation button, and updates on conversation_created/updated/deleted.
Resuming a conversation (openConversation) restores persona, route pin, privacy tags, and enabled tool servers into the active session state.
app.tsx assembles all five surfaces into a navigable layout with a SINGLE top-level onCoreEvent subscription that fans events into the stores and cleans up on unmount.
capabilities/default.json remains least-privilege (core:default; no fs/shell/network to the webview) with its description updated for the Phase 5 command set; it is valid JSON.
README 'Implementation status' shows Phase 5 as DONE with a short summary, matching the Phases 0-4 convention.
vitest/RTL tests cover the history surface and the app shell (rendering, mocked-invoke calls, event fan-out, unlisten on unmount).
`NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check .` passes across the whole frontend.
verification: Run `NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check .` from hybrid-orchestrator/frontend; confirm the whole frontend is clean.
Confirm capabilities/default.json is valid JSON and README shows Phase 5 DONE.
Self-audit ESLint/tsc; report the exact local-vs-CI check matrix in findings (prettier local; eslint/tsc/vitest + all cargo per-crate checks on CI).
